pairs.subject: invariant-placement
pairs.evidence: scripts/ci/flake-check.mjs:273 loadRuns silently skips any run record that fails to parse or lacks `tests`/`startedAt`, and nothing counts the skips: the transitions predicate (line 321) reports only the survivors, and a schema drift in flake-record that empties every record is printed as 'NONE RECORDED YET'. The repair erases the evidence that records were dropped.

techniques.evidence: scripts/ci/flake-check.mjs:273 Swallow-and-continue repair that is expected to fire, but no firing count is emitted and no test covers it; the predicate counts survivors only. Contrast: disk-check's self-heal does print what it pruned and a test asserts /Pruned/ (disk-check.test.mjs:316), and --no-prune keeps the pure verdict.

scripts/ci/flake-id.mjs:301 When the resolver (targetForRunningPath) returns null, the caller writes a sentinel into the test-identity space. Unresolved tests from different binaries that share a module path then merge into one history key, which the module's own header calls 'worse than having none'. The docstring (lines 271-273) says these records carry `target: null`, but the code emits no target field, and no test exercises this path. lane-certify's cannot-see/cannot-run verdicts are honest members: they have producers and consumers that act on them differently.

scripts/ci/flake-record.mjs:197 The emitted run record defaults an absent branch to the plausible string 'unknown', while the next field (sha) correctly uses null. transitions() filters on branch === 'master', so such a record silently drops out of history. Positive counterpart: lane-certify sends every verdict through one `emit` door (lane-certify.mjs:283) and writes measurement, criteria and verdict together.

scripts/ci/lane-certify.test.mjs:402 The cross-file invariant (canary constant PLANTED in lane-canary.mjs vs the `max` in .lanes/criteria.json) is computed rather than left to the 'by construction' comment, on the fast harness rung rather than only in the nightly lane.

scripts/ci/lane-certify.test.mjs:315 The canary inversion was raised from four call sites into one emit door. Negative tests whose pass condition is a refusal cover its no-artifact, pass and missing-metric exits, and mcp-gate-parity.test guards its mutation fixtures against going vacuous (`mutation did not apply — fixture is stale`). The canary no-criteria path is untested.
scripts/ci/flake-check.mjs:328 The 'flaky' label is computed from same-commit transitions on every run, never declared. labels.json is a regenerated cache, not a second source.

scripts/ci/mcp-gate-parity.mjs:41 The checker names the altitude the rule belongs at (one authority) and declares itself the interim floor (line 42). The three hand-written copies themselves live in crates/server/src/mcp/mod.rs, outside this context.

scripts/ci/mcp-gate-parity.mjs:27 The context's checker rules are arrangement/vocabulary-parity rules (MCP sites, register-vs-tree reconciliation), not terms about identity, capture time, consumption or read set.

scripts/ci/flake-check.mjs:388 Bring-up (register read, scanner liveness) has exactly one caller, main(). The technique's own exception says to assert the precondition there, and the code does, exiting 3.

scripts/ci/flake-check.mjs:462 There is no single-use value. The only once-per-key obligation (one size sample per day) is per-identity, and it is enforced at the store write, as the technique prescribes.

scripts/ci/flake-check.mjs:271 Writer (flake-record, or the Rust lane harness) and reader (flake-check, lane-certify) are separate processes or languages. The technique excludes that case as a contract, not a pair of checks.
scripts/ci/disk-check.mjs:263 Untyped JS with no structural checker, and no encoding claims to make a state unrepresentable. Same-typed budget members are passed by named key rather than position.

pairs.registryProposal: shape-with-a-not-applicable-member is framed around exhaustiveness compelling consumers to write arms. Dynamic-language code has a sibling form with a different harm: a sentinel segment written into a composite string key (`unknown::unknown::<name>`). No arms are compelled; instead, unrelated values merge under one key. The technique could name this variant and its audit (enumerate the producers of the sentinel, then check whether any consumer aggregates by that key).
